description: Conditional no-contact lease consumption after actual timeout: pipeline path and ordinary comparison, each with its own constructed local prefix.

harness.description: Two independent local operations. Construct two-voter Leader and expired peer marker; actual in-memory transport admits an unanswered request. Pipeline case awaits actual future error and runs actual pipelineDecode to completion; ordinary case runs replicateTo to completion. Inspect admitted request without responding, then invoke actual checkLeaderLease and emit public State. No full Raft workers or election prefix.
semantic_changes: Construct local Raft state directly rather than bootstrap/elect; this is the accepted conditional premise.
Receiver transport has no receiver Raft worker and sends no response. This prevents new contact independently of the tested marker.
Call pipelineDecode/replicateTo and checkLeaderLease explicitly; omit main loop, heartbeat, snapshots and verification to isolate effect. This does not establish deployed role retention.
Read LastContact under its lock and State through public API; only emit measured fields and declared setup. No protocol source is modified.

legality.derivation: Constructor and pipeline APIs admit requests. With a buffered receiver transport and no receiver Raft, admitted input can time out without remote processing or response. Local Leader state and expired contact are conditional initial premises; no claim that constructor alone establishes them. One queued request per separate transport pair fixes identity; pipeline returned future.Request is compared to that exact request. Completion precedes lease consumption in each operation.
legality.applicability: Fixed two Voters, expired four-second-old marker and two-second lease. Real forty-millisecond timeout; isolated local comparison only.
unresolved: Proof of a legal election/startup history
Automatic lease scheduling or total role-retention duration
Application stale reads, client success, or incorrect log commitment
alternatives: Ordinary replicateTo propagates transport timeout and preserves old contact.
Heartbeat replies, including negative replies, can constitute actual contact; not excluded by this obligation.
Fallback replication, incoming RPCs and negative VerifyLeader responses may force role loss independently; their absence is explicit local scope.

grounding.derivation: Config.LeaderLeaseTimeout explicitly promises step-down when the interval elapses without quorum contact. For two Voters, self alone is insufficient. With prior remote contact already expired and an unanswered request never processed by a receiver, no new remote contact exists. Therefore after the timeout consumer completes, a lease decision must not count that completion as contact and must step down. AppendFuture.Response additionally restricts validity to successful Error completion, supporting rejection of failed-future response fields as evidence, but the observed endpoint comparison is the lease decision rather than just API usage. The oracle does not come from the pipeline-versus-ordinary difference.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the actual in-repository in-memory transport implementation and actual checkLeaderLease consumer under stated conditional premises. The config contract is public; its implementation uses contact recency and majority of Voters. A rejected real reply may still be contact and is outside the no-reply antecedent.
unresolved: Whether this conditional prefix occurs in one legal full-node history with protective workers active.
Whether a single refresh postpones externally observable leadership loss; the local invocation alone establishes neither a timing bound nor an application failure.
alternatives: Ordinary replicateTo propagates transport timeout and preserves old contact.
Heartbeat replies, including negative replies, can constitute actual contact; not excluded by this obligation.
Fallback replication, incoming RPCs and negative VerifyLeader responses may force role loss independently; their absence is explicit local scope.

observable_properties.description: For each completed isolated no-contact timeout scenario with constructed expired-contact Leader prefix, the subsequent actual lease decision must produce Follower. Leader is the forbidden endpoint; timeout of the test does not count as a violation.

uncertainties: Proof of a legal election/startup history
Automatic lease scheduling or total role-retention duration
Application stale reads, client success, or incorrect log commitment
Operation labels associate separate scenarios, not one shared history.
The prior contact is constructed as expired; no legal full-node initial prefix is proved.
No claim that rejecting a real heartbeat response is required: no-response and negative-response are different contexts.
